questions.question:
D4 — Does this first-person narrative match what your ML engineer experiences today?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: Before scoring anything, I walk the actual README path as the target developer and describe what they see and feel. If I have the experience wrong, every score downstream is wrong too, so please correct me here. Stakes: this narrative becomes the Developer Perspective section the implementer reads.

NARRATIVE (ML engineer, terminal, wants a local result before CI):
I open the README. Heading one is "EvalKit SDK", and the first paragraph describes me exactly, so I keep reading. Under "Getting started" I copy `python -m pip install evalkit==2.0.0b1`, export EVALKIT_API_KEY, and run `python examples/first_eval.py` as instructed. Python says "No such file or directory". I check site-packages: evalkit has client.py, demo.py, sample_responses.json, no examples folder. Thirty seconds lost, some trust lost. The next paragraph mentions `python -m evalkit.demo`, so I try that. It starts, then stderr prints "Waiting for CI check: 30s elapsed of 300s". I wanted a local score on bundled sample data; instead I'm waiting five minutes on a remote check I never configured, at 30-second updates, with no flag to skip it. Peer SDK A gave me a number in two minutes total. I alt-tab. Later the scores appear: 0.80, 1.00, 0.90. Fine. I write my own call: `run_eval(dataset, evaluator)`. Then I try `run_batch(dataset, evaluator)` and it fails, because run_batch takes (evaluator, dataset). I paste a typo'd key and get `AuthError("request failed")`: no code, no hint that the key is the problem. On my existing v1 code, `Client.evaluate()` is now simply gone with no warning or migration note.

Stakes if we pick wrong: the review polishes the wrong pain.
Recommendation: A because every step above traces to a specific line in README.md, docs/api.md, docs/current-contracts.md, or docs/package-contents.txt.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: proceed on the traced path vs. correct it before scoring.

options.label: Accurate, proceed (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Every beat is grounded in a documented contract, not a guess about the runtime. ✅ Lets the review move to friction-point decisions immediately. ❌ If the runtime differs from the docs, the scores inherit that gap.

options.label: Some of this is wrong
options.description: ✅ You correct specific beats (for example, the demo may not need an API key) before scoring. ✅ Keeps the narrative honest for the implementer who reads it. ❌ Costs one round-trip before friction-point questions begin.

options.label: Way off, actual experience is...
options.description: ✅ Replaces the narrative entirely with your account of the real first run. ✅ Prevents a review built on a wrong premise. ❌ Discards the traced path and requires you to describe the flow from scratch.

questions.question:
D5 — Journey stage HELLO WORLD: the mandatory 5-minute CI check on the first local evaluation. Fix in plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: docs/current-contracts.md lines 3-5 say every developer's first local evaluation blocks five minutes on a successful remote CI check, with no skip flag or offline path, and README.md line 17-18 says the demo waits on it too. docs/benchmarks.md measures 6 minutes total, 5 of them this wait; the agreed target is under 2 minutes. This is a mandatory server-side check imposed on a local run of bundled sample data, for a persona who wants a local result before connecting CI. The existing SDK already has offline sample data and a mock transport (current-contracts.md line 18), so an offline first run needs no new service. Stakes: this one gate is the entire gap between Needs Work tier and Champion tier.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the terminal demo's magical moment arrives five minutes late and the study's target stays unmet at release.
Recommendation: A because the demo and first local run should use the already-shipped offline data and mock transport; the CI check belongs to the CI integration step the persona reaches later, not to hello world.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10, D=0/10
Net: move the CI check to where CI actually happens vs. keep blocking local first runs and hope the progress line holds attention.

options.label: Remove gate from local first run (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Demo and first local evaluation return scores in about a minute using existing offline data and mock transport; TTHW drops from 6 min to ~1 min. ✅ CI check still runs, but only when the developer enters CI/noninteractive mode or first submits a remote job. ❌ Requires an SDK runtime change in the separate repo and a doc update (human: ~2 days / CC: ~30 min).

options.label: Keep gate, add skip flag
options.description: ✅ Adds EVALKIT_SKIP_CI_CHECK / --skip-ci-check so an informed developer can bypass the wait. ✅ Smaller runtime change; default behavior stays as documented. ❌ Default path still takes 6 minutes; the persona has to read docs to find the flag, which the persona does not do (human: ~1 day / CC: ~15 min).

options.label: Keep gate, improve messaging
options.description: ✅ Progress line explains why the check exists and what it verifies. ✅ No runtime behavior change beyond text. ❌ Time to first result stays 6 minutes, three times the agreed target; peer SDKs remain 2-4 minutes.

options.label: Acceptable friction, skip
options.description: ✅ Zero work; ships exactly the documented contract. ✅ Keeps the CI guarantee identical for every run. ❌ Leaves the plan knowingly failing its own onboarding target with the largest measured cause untouched.

answers.D5 \u2014 Journey stage HELLO WORLD: the: Remove gate from local first run (recommended)

questions.question:
D7 — Journey stage REAL USAGE: run_eval(dataset, evaluator) and run_batch(evaluator, dataset) take the same two arguments in opposite positional order. Fix in plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: docs/api.md lines 3-9: the two public evaluation functions accept the same concepts positionally but reversed, neither requires keywords, and the plan keeps this on purpose. A developer who learned run_eval will call run_batch with arguments swapped. Because both are plain positional objects, the failure is either a confusing type error deep inside or, worse, a silently wrong evaluation. Stakes: this is the SDK's core call; inconsistency here is the kind of thing developers screenshot and post.
Stakes if we pick wrong: swapped-argument bugs in production evaluation pipelines that are hard to spot in review.
Recommendation: A because one order across both functions plus keyword acceptance removes the trap entirely, and a one-release shim keeps existing 2.0.0b1 callers working.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=4/10, D=0/10
Net: consistent signatures with a bridge vs. keeping the trap and warning about it in prose.

options.label: Unify order, keyword-friendly, shim (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Both functions become (dataset, evaluator) and accept keywords; run_batch detects the legacy (evaluator, dataset) order by type and emits a DeprecationWarning for one beta cycle. ✅ Type annotations already exist, so mypy and IDEs flag the old order (human: ~1 day / CC: ~20 min). ❌ A runtime change in the SDK repo plus a changelog entry, during a beta.

options.label: Keyword-only arguments
options.description: ✅ Add a bare * so dataset= and evaluator= are required; order can no longer be wrong. ✅ Simple to implement and self-documenting at every call site. ❌ Breaks every existing positional caller of both functions at once with no bridge (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min).

options.label: Document the difference
options.description: ✅ docs/api.md and docstrings state the order prominently with a warning. ✅ No runtime change. ❌ The persona copies code, does not read reference docs, and the trap remains live.

options.label: Acceptable friction, skip
options.description: ✅ Ships the documented signatures unchanged. ✅ Zero implementation effort. ❌ Locks an inconsistent public API into the 2.0 line, where fixing it later costs a major version.

questions.question:
D8 — Journey stage DEBUG: an invalid API key raises AuthError("request failed") with no code, cause, or fix. Fix in plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: docs/api.md lines 11-13: a bad key produces the message "request failed" and nothing else, and the plan keeps it. docs/current-contracts.md lines 11-14 say every OTHER error already names the cause, the argument or file involved, and an actionable fix, and redacts secrets. So auth is the one error that breaks the SDK's own error contract, and it is the error a brand-new developer is most likely to hit first (typo in EVALKIT_API_KEY, wrong environment, expired key). Stakes: "request failed" sends the developer to a search engine or a support inbox for a ten-second fix.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the first real error a new user sees looks like a network outage instead of a fixable config mistake.
Recommendation: A because it brings AuthError up to the standard the other errors already meet; no new error framework is needed.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10, D=0/10
Net: bring auth in line with the existing error contract vs. leave the most common first error as the only unhelpful one.

options.label: Full problem/cause/fix error (recommended)
options.description: ✅ AuthError carries a stable code (e.g. EVALKIT_AUTH_INVALID_KEY), says the key from EVALKIT_API_KEY was rejected, tells the developer where to get or rotate a key, and links to docs; key value redacted, HTTP status kept. ✅ Matches the existing contract every other error meets (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min). ❌ Touches the SDK runtime and the API doc; needs a test that the key never appears in the message.

options.label: Better message only
options.description: ✅ Replace "request failed" with "Invalid API key. Check EVALKIT_API_KEY." ✅ Smallest possible runtime diff. ❌ No stable code for programmatic handling and no link to key management, so CI logs still need a human to interpret them.

options.label: Document the error in a troubleshooting section
options.description: ✅ README or docs/api.md explains what "request failed" usually means. ✅ No runtime change. ❌ The developer must leave the terminal and guess that a generic message maps to an auth entry.

options.label: Acceptable friction, skip
options.description: ✅ Ships the documented message unchanged. ✅ Zero effort. ❌ Leaves one public error knowingly below the SDK's own documented error standard.

questions.question:
D9 — Journey stage UPGRADE: v2 removes Client.evaluate() immediately in favor of Client.run(), with no alias, warning, migration guide, or codemod. Fix in plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: docs/api.md lines 15-18: every v1 user who upgrades gets AttributeError on the first call, with nothing telling them the method was renamed. The changelog is otherwise complete, so this is the one upgrade hazard. Upgrade fear is the reason teams pin old versions forever; upgrades should be boring. Stakes: the existing user base is the group most likely to give beta feedback, and this is the first thing they hit.
Stakes if we pick wrong: production pipelines break on upgrade and the beta earns a "breaks without warning" reputation.
Recommendation: A because a deprecated alias plus a migration note costs a few lines and turns a hard break into a warning the developer fixes on their own schedule.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=4/10, D=0/10
Net: soft landing with a scheduled removal vs. a hard break with better paperwork.

options.label: Deprecated alias + migration guide (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Client.evaluate() stays as a thin wrapper that emits DeprecationWarning naming Client.run() and the removal version; changelog gets a Migrating from v1 section with the one-line rename. ✅ Existing code keeps running; the rename is a sed, so a codemod is optional (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min). ❌ Carries one legacy name for one more release cycle.

options.label: Remove now, guided AttributeError + guide
options.description: ✅ Override __getattr__ so client.evaluate raises an error that says use Client.run(); add the migration section to the changelog. ✅ No legacy surface survives into 2.0. ❌ Still a hard break on upgrade; every v1 caller must change code before anything runs.

options.label: Changelog note only
options.description: ✅ One paragraph in the changelog documents the rename. ✅ No runtime change. ❌ The developer only learns about it after the AttributeError sends them to read release notes.

options.label: Acceptable friction, skip
options.description: ✅ Ships the documented behavior unchanged. ✅ Zero effort. ❌ Every upgrading user hits an unexplained failure on their first call.

questions.question:
D10 — First-time developer roleplay: which confusion points should the plan address?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: I replayed the getting-started flow as your ML engineer with a clock running, using only the README and docs as they ship today. Each numbered item is a moment of confusion grounded in a specific line. Stakes: whatever we leave here ships to every beta user on day one.

FIRST-TIME DEVELOPER REPORT
Persona: ML engineer, Python daily, terminal, wants local result before CI
Attempting: EvalKit 2.0.0b1 getting started
T+0:00  Read README para 1. "That's me." Copy pip install line. Installs fine.
T+0:30  #1 README says set EVALKIT_API_KEY before anything. I don't have a key yet and the README never says where to get one or whether the demo needs it. I dig one up from a teammate.
T+1:00  #2 Run `python examples/first_eval.py` per README line 11. "No such file or directory." Check site-packages, no examples dir (package-contents.txt).
T+1:30  Spot `python -m evalkit.demo` one paragraph down. Run it.
T+1:45  #3 stderr: "Waiting for CI check: 30s elapsed of 300s". What CI? I haven't set up CI. No flag to skip. I open Slack.
T+6:45  Scores print: 0.80, 1.00, 0.90. Matches README. Six minutes and forty-five seconds to the magical moment; peer SDK A took two.
T+8:00  #4 Write my own run_eval(dataset, evaluator). Works. Try run_batch(dataset, evaluator). Fails; docs/api.md says run_batch is (evaluator, dataset).
T+9:00  #5 Fat-finger the key. AuthError("request failed"). Assume the service is down. Check status page. It isn't.
T+10:00 #6 Point old v1 pipeline at 2.0.0b1. AttributeError: Client has no attribute evaluate. Nothing tells me it became run().
Final state: succeeded, irritated, would not recommend yet.

#2 through #6 are already fixed by D5-D9. #1 is new: the README does not say where to obtain a key or whether the demo needs one.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a stale confusion survives into the beta README.
Recommendation: A because #1 is a README-only fix that fits DX POLISH and the other five are already in the plan.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=depends, C=8/10, D=0/10
Net: close the last README gap now vs. leave key acquisition undocumented.

options.label: All of them (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Adds a one-line "get a key at <URL>" step and states whether the demo needs a key, closing #1; #2-#6 already in plan. ✅ README becomes fully self-sufficient for the first five minutes (human: ~1 hour / CC: ~5 min). ❌ One more README edit to coordinate with the key-management URL owner.

options.label: Let me pick
options.description: ✅ You choose which of #1-#6 stay in scope. ✅ Useful if key acquisition is deliberately out of the README (for example, enterprise provisioning). ❌ One more round-trip before scoring begins.

options.label: Critical only (#2, #3)
options.description: ✅ Keeps the two adoption blockers, the broken quickstart and the CI wait. ✅ Smallest release diff. ❌ Reverses D7-D9 decisions already made and leaves #1 open.

options.label: Unrealistic, our devs already know
options.description: ✅ No further README work. ✅ Assumes every beta user is an existing customer with a key in hand. ❌ New evaluators arriving from the README still stall at T+0:30 with no key source.

questions.question:
D11 — Enable cross-project learnings search on this machine?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, before the eight DX scoring passes.
ELI10: gstack can search learnings saved from your other projects on this machine to find patterns that might apply here. Everything stays local; no data leaves the machine. Recommended for solo developers. Skip if you work across multiple client codebases where cross-contamination would be a concern. Stakes if we pick wrong: either missed reusable lessons or an unwanted cross-client leak inside your own machine's notes.
Recommendation: A because this is a single-developer sandbox with no client separation signal, and the flag can be flipped later with gstack-config.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: broader recall of past lessons vs. strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Future reviews surface patterns learned on your other local projects automatically. ✅ Stays local; reversible with gstack-config set cross_project_learnings false. ❌ Notes from unrelated projects can appear in a client codebase session.

options.label: Keep project-scoped only
options.description: ✅ Strict isolation between codebases, safest for multi-client work. ✅ Nothing from this fixture leaks into other projects' reviews. ❌ Loses reuse of lessons already learned elsewhere on this machine.

questions.question:

Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: Today README "Getting started" (lines 10-11) reads install, set EVALKIT_API_KEY, run a missing file. options.description: ✅ Keeps the current step order and only adds the "where to get a key" line from D10. ✅ No runtime change to the demo. ❌ The first two minutes include a credential hunt for a command that evaluates local sample data (human: ~30 min / CC: ~5 min).

options.label: Keep README order, document only

questions.question:
D13 — Pass 3 Error Messages (4/10 today, 9/10 after D7-D9): should the CI-wait progress line say what is being checked and how to inspect it?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-4dncQn on main, EvalKit SDK beta polish.
ELI10: docs/current-contracts.md lines 7-8: during the CI check the SDK prints "Waiting for CI check: 90s elapsed of 300s" to stderr every 30 seconds. After D5 this line only appears on the first CI-mode or remote run, which is the right place for it. But the line still fails the Hall of Fame formula (what happened + why + how to fix + where to learn more): it says how long, not what is being verified, where the check runs, or what to do if it exceeds 300 s. In a CI log that is the difference between "the SDK is doing X, here is the run URL" and a five-minute stall with no explanation. Stakes: this is the SDK's longest-lived user-visible message; it should explain itself.
Stakes if we pick wrong: platform engineers reading CI logs cannot tell a healthy first-run check from a hang.
Recommendation: A because the change is a message template plus a documented timeout outcome, no behavior change to the check itself.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=0/10
Net: self-explaining wait vs. a bare countdown.

options.label: Explain the check in the line (recommended)
options.description: ✅ First line states what is being verified and where (e.g. "First CI run: verifying project <id> against EvalKit CI check <url>; typically completes in under 5 min"), later lines keep the elapsed/total countdown. ✅ On timeout, the error names the check URL and the fix (retry, check status page), matching the other errors' contract (human: ~2 hours / CC: ~10 min). ❌ Touches the SDK runtime message templates and docs/current-contracts.md.

options.label: Add a one-line preface only
options.description: ✅ Prints a single explanatory line before the existing countdown; the countdown text stays as documented. ✅ Smallest runtime diff. ❌ Timeout path still ends without a documented what-next.

options.label: Acceptable as is
options.description: ✅ No change; the countdown already shows progress. ✅ Zero effort. ❌ The only long-running message in the SDK remains the one that does not explain itself.

answers.D13 \u2014 Pass 3 Error Messages (4/10 t: Explain the check in the line (recommended)
